chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), similar to it.
Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said regarding the one who performs li'an:
If he admits his lie before the cursing, his wife is returned to him, and he is whipped the limit; and if he refuses, he curses, and she does not become permissible to him ever.
And if a man accuses his wife, upon him is the limit; and if his child dies, his maternal uncles inherit him.
So if his father claims him, he is attached to him; and if he dies, the son inherits him, and the father does not inherit him.
ai.seo_question: What are the inheritance and marital consequences for a child of li'an if the father admits his false accusation?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the procedural nuances of li'an, distinguishing between pre-cursing admission of falsehood, which restores the marriage, and persistent denial, which enforces permanent separation. It further clarifies the unique inheritance dynamics for the child of li'an, where the maternal uncles inherit the child, yet the father is excluded from inheriting the child, highlighting the severance of paternal lineage ties in this specific legal context.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Musa Bin Bakr, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, similar to it’.
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said regarding a cursing one who (admitted) having lied to himself before the cursing (his wife): ‘His wife would be returned to him, and he would be whipped the Limit, and if he refuses and curses (anyway), his wife would not be Permissible to him, ever.
And if a man accuses his wife, upon him would be the Limit (of Punishment), and if his child dies, his maternal uncle would inherit him.
So if his father claims him, he would be attached with him, and if the inheritors of the son die, his father would not inherit him’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has narrated the following: “This is about the case of a man who decides to proceed with condemnation.

He then calls himself as lying before the process of condemnation. Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘His woman is returned to him, he is made to suffer the applicable penalty; but if he refuses and proceeds with condemnation process she will never become lawful for him.
If a man accuses his woman, he must suffer the penalty. If his son dies, his maternal uncle inherits him.
If his father claims him, he is joined with him. If he dies his son inherits him but his father cannot inherit him (the son).”’
